claim: Fungi employ LysM effectors to prevent recognition of cell wall-derived chitin by host immune receptors.
source_text: Fungi employ LysM effectors to prevent recognition of cell wall-derived chitin by host immune receptors, although the mechanism to compete for chitin binding remained unclear.
evidence_reasoning: This is a general statement about fungal LysM effectors that draws from established scientific knowledge in the field and is supported by the broader literature context.

claim: Ecp6 binds chitin through intrachain LysM dimerization involving two of its three LysM domains.
source_text: Structural analysis of the LysM effector Ecp6 of the fungal tomato pathogen Cladosporium fulvum reveals a novel mechanism for chitin binding, mediated by intrachain LysM dimerization
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by the crystal structure data presented in the manuscript, including Figure 1 showing the structural analysis.

claim: The composite LysM1-LysM3 binding site of Ecp6 mediates chitin binding with ultra-high picomolar affinity.
source_text: This composite binding site involves two of the three LysMs of Ecp6 and mediates chitin binding with ultra-high (pM) affinity.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the ITC experimental data showing picomolar affinity binding constants for chitin-free Ecp6 produced in HEK293 cells.

claim: The singular LysM2 domain of Ecp6 binds chitin with low micromolar affinity.
source_text: Intriguingly, the remaining singular LysM domain of Ecp6 binds chitin with low micromolar affinity but can nevertheless still perturb chitin-triggered immunity.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by ITC measurements showing micromolar binding affinity for P. pastoris-produced Ecp6 where only LysM2 is available for binding.

claim: LysM2 may perturb chitin-triggered immunity through interference with the host immune receptor complex rather than through chitin sequestration.
source_text: Conceivably, the perturbation by this LysM domain is not established through chitin sequestration but possibly through interference with the host immune receptor complex.
evidence_reasoning: This is explicitly stated as a speculative mechanism ('conceivably', 'possibly') inferred from the observation that LysM2 suppresses immunity despite low affinity.

claim: Chitin is the primary structural component of fungal cell walls.
source_text: Chitin, an N-acetyl-D-glucosamine (GlcNAc) homopolymer, is the primary structural component of fungal cell walls
evidence_reasoning: This is established scientific knowledge about fungal cell wall composition.

claim: Chitin is recognized as a PAMP by plant cell surface receptors containing extracellular lysin motifs (LysMs).
source_text: Chitin, an N-acetyl-D-glucosamine (GlcNAc) homopolymer, is the primary structural component of fungal cell walls and is recognized as a PAMP by plant cell surface receptors that contain extracellular lysin motifs (LysMs)
evidence_reasoning: This statement is supported by multiple citations (Felix et al., 1993; Shibuya et al., 1993; Shibuya et al., 1996; Kombrink et al., 2011) and represents established knowledge.

claim: Rice CEBiP was the first cloned chitin receptor and forms a ligand-dependent receptor complex with OsCERK1.
source_text: The first chitin receptor has been cloned from rice (Oryza sativa) as the chitin oligosaccharide elicitor-binding protein (CEBiP; Kaku et al., 2006) that forms a receptor complex in a ligand-dependent manner that furthermore includes the chitin elicitor receptor kinase-1 (OsCERK1; Shimizu et al., 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by citations to the original research papers (Kaku et al., 2006; Shimizu et al., 2010).

claim: Arabidopsis thaliana CERK1 binds chitin and is required for chitin-triggered immunity.
source_text: Similarly, Arabidopsis thaliana CERK1 binds chitin and is required for chitin-triggered immunity (Miya et al., 2007; Wan et al., 2008; Iizasa et al., 2010; Petutschnig et al., 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by multiple citations to published research demonstrating CERK1's role in chitin recognition.

claim: LysM2 of AtCERK1 binds three GlcNAc residues of a chitin oligomer in a shallow groove on the protein surface.
source_text: LysM2 of AtCERK1 binds three GlcNAc residues of a longer chitin oligomer in a shallow groove on the surface of the protein, with both ends of the oligomer as well as one half side of each of the three bound GlcNAc residues protruding into the solvent (Liu et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on the crystal structure reported by Liu et al., 2012 (PDB code 4EBZ).

claim: Sufficiently long chitin oligomers act as bivalent ligands leading to ligand-induced AtCERK1 dimerization required for immune signaling.
source_text: Biochemical experiments suggest that sufficiently long chitin oligomers act as bivalent ligands, leading to ligand-induced AtCERK1 dimerization that is required for immune signaling (Liu et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This is based on biochemical experiments reported in Liu et al., 2012.

claim: Cladosporium fulvum abundantly secretes the LysM-containing effector protein Ecp6 during colonization of tomato.
source_text: The leaf mold fungus Cladosporium fulvum abundantly secretes the LysM-containing effector protein Ecp6 (for extracellular protein 6; Bolton et al., 2008) during colonization of its host tomato.
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the citation to Bolton et al., 2008.

claim: Ecp6 acts as a scavenger of chitin fragments to prevent recognition by host immune receptors.
source_text: Ecp6 acts as a scavenger of chitin fragments and thus prevents recognition of the fungus by host immune receptors (de Jonge et al., 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the citation to de Jonge et al., 2010.

claim: Ecp6 homologs occur throughout the fungal kingdom.
source_text: Intriguingly, Ecp6 homologs occur throughout the fungal kingdom, suggesting a fundamental role of chitin scavenging in fungal pathogenicity (Bolton et al., 2008; de Jonge and Thomma, 2009).
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Bolton et al., 2008 and de Jonge and Thomma, 2009.

claim: LysM effectors from Mycosphaerella graminicola and Magnaporthe oryzae suppress chitin-triggered immunity.
source_text: Indeed, LysM effectors from the fungal wheat pathogen Mycosphaerella graminicola and the rice pathogen Magnaporthe oryzae suppress chitin-triggered immunity (Marshall et al., 2011; Mentlak et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by citations to Marshall et al., 2011 and Mentlak et al., 2012.

claim: The canonical three-dimensional LysM domain structure consists of a βααβ-fold.
source_text: The canonical three-dimensional LysM domain structure consists of a βααβ-fold, in which two α-helices are packed against one side of a two-stranded antiparallel β-sheet.
evidence_reasoning: This describes the established structural motif of LysM domains based on previous structural studies.

claim: LysM domains interact with chitin oligomers in a 1:1 stoichiometry with an affinity binding constant of up to 21 µM.
source_text: Based on NMR spectroscopy, the loop between the first β-sheet and the first α-helix and the loop between the second α-helix and the second β-sheet were shown to physically interact with chitin oligomers in a 1:1 stoichiometry with an affinity binding constant of up to 21 µM (Ohnuma et al., 2008; Koharudin et al., 2011).
evidence_reasoning: This is based on NMR spectroscopy studies cited from Ohnuma et al., 2008 and Koharudin et al., 2011.

claim: The AtCERK1 ectodomain binds chitin oligomers with an affinity up to 45 µM for (GlcNAc)8.
source_text: The AtCERK1 ectodomain binds chitin oligomers with a similar affinity, up to 45 µM for (GlcNAc)8, as determined by isothermal titration calorimetry (Liu et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This is based on ITC measurements reported in Liu et al., 2012.

claim: The crystal structure of Ecp6 was determined to a resolution of 1.6 Å.
source_text: Here, we report the crystal structure of Ecp6 to a resolution of 1.6 Å
evidence_reasoning: This is directly supported by the crystallographic data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Ecp6 has a tightly packed structure stabilized by four disulfide bridges.
source_text: Ecp6 has a tightly packed structure that is stabilized by four disulfide bridges
evidence_reasoning: This is observed directly in the crystal structure data (Figure 1A).

claim: Two spatially close glycosylation sites were identified in Ecp6 at Asn104 and Asn193.
source_text: two spatially close glycosylation sites (Asn104 and Asn193) were identified
evidence_reasoning: This is identified from the crystal structure analysis.

claim: The three LysMs of Ecp6 share the typical βααβ-fold.
source_text: The three LysMs of Ecp6 (LysM1–LysM3) share the typical βααβ-fold
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in the crystal structure data.

claim: LysM1 is separated by a long and flexible linker from a compact and rigid body formed by LysM2 and LysM3.
source_text: with LysM1 being separated by a long and flexible linker from a compact and rigid body formed by LysM2 and LysM3
evidence_reasoning: This structural feature is observed in the crystal structure (Figure 1A).

claim: Crystal packing revealed the existence of an Ecp6 homodimer with a buried surface of 943 Å2 at LysM2 and LysM3.
source_text: Furthermore, the crystal packing revealed the existence of an Ecp6 homodimer that was also observed in gel filtration chromatography during protein purification, with a flat buried surface of 943 Å2 at LysM2 and LysM3
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by both crystallographic data and gel filtration chromatography observations.

claim: A chitin tetramer (GlcNAc)4 was found bound in a large interdomain groove between LysM1 and LysM3.
source_text: Unexpectedly, the calculated 2Fo−Fc map showed a well-defined electron density for a bound chitin tetramer (GlcNAc)4 in a large interdomain groove between LysM1 and LysM3 (∼16 Å long and ∼11 Å across its widest points; Figure 1B)
evidence_reasoning: This is directly observed in the electron density map from the crystal structure.

claim: The chitin oligomer co-purified with Ecp6 was likely derived from the cell wall of the P. pastoris expression system.
source_text: The chitin oligomer was likely co-purified with Ecp6 and derived from the cell wall of the P. pastoris expression system.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the fact that chitin was found bound despite no exogenous chitin being added during crystallization.

claim: The chitin tetramer in the LysM1-LysM3 groove is engaged in 12 hydrogen bonds with Ecp6.
source_text: Evidently, LysM1 and LysM3 of Ecp6 cooperate to bring two chitin-binding regions together, composing a novel type of binding groove in which one chitin tetramer is nearly completely buried and engaged in many noncovalent interactions, including 12 hydrogen bonds (Figure 1C).
evidence_reasoning: This is determined from the crystal structure analysis showing specific interactions (Figure 1C).

claim: The chitin-binding groove is shaped by amino acids 20GDTLT24 and 46PNLIEL51 of LysM1 and 150GDLFV154 and 176PSKL179 of LysM3.
source_text: Specifically, the groove is shaped by the amino acids 20GDTLT24 and 46PNLIEL51 of LysM1 and 150GDLFV154 and 176PSKL179 of LysM3.
evidence_reasoning: This is identified from the crystal structure showing which residues form the binding groove.

claim: All Ecp6 mutants in LysM1 and LysM3 were able to bind chitin according to ITC analysis.
source_text: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) analysis demonstrated that all mutants were able to bind chitin
evidence_reasoning: This is directly demonstrated by the ITC experimental data presented in Figure 3.

claim: Mutants in LysM3 (L152R and S177K) showed reduced chitin-binding affinity compared to wild-type Ecp6.
source_text: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) analysis demonstrated that all mutants were able to bind chitin
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the ITC data in Figure 3 showing different binding curves for the mutants compared to wild-type.

claim: Mutants L152R and S177K in LysM3 were impaired in suppressing chitin-triggered immunity in tomato cells.
source_text: the two mutants in LysM3 (L152R and S177K) were impaired in prevention of chitin-triggered alkalinization of tomato cell suspensions
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by the alkalinization assay data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Mutants T22R and N47K in LysM1 resulted in an autoactive protein that triggered a response in tomato cells in the absence of chitin.
source_text: Unfortunately, the two mutants that were generated in LysM1 (T22R and N47K) resulted in an autoactive protein that triggered a response of the tomato cells, leading to medium alkalinization already in the absence of chitin
evidence_reasoning: This is observed in the alkalinization assay experiments (Figure 4A).

claim: Circular dichroism analysis showed that mutants L152R and S177K retained proper folding.
source_text: Circular dichroism spectra of the mutants in LysM1 (B) and LysM3 (D) at 10 µM.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the CD spectra shown in Figure 4D indicating proper secondary structure.

claim: LysM2 mutants T95R and D121K were impaired in chitin binding.
source_text: T95R and (D) D121K mutants on LysM2 are impaired in chitin binding.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by ITC experiments shown in Figure 5C and 5D.

claim: LysM2 mutants T95R and D121K retained proper folding as shown by circular dichroism.
source_text: Circular dichroism spectra of the mutants on LysM2 at 10 µM.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the CD spectra in Figure 5B showing characteristic secondary structure.

claim: LysM2 mutants T95R and D121K were impaired in suppressing chitin-triggered immunity.
source_text: P. pastoris-produced LysM2 mutants in Ecp6 were impaired in prevention of chitin-triggered alkalinization of tomato cell suspensions (Figure 5).
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by the alkalinization assay data in Figure 5A.

claim: Chitin-free Ecp6 was successfully produced in mammalian HEK293 cells.
source_text: As an alternative strategy, the production of Ecp6 in mammalian (HEK293) cells was pursued. A relatively small amount (4 mg) of chitin-free Ecp6 was obtained from these cells.
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct report of the experimental production method and outcome.

claim: Ecp6 produced in HEK293 cells was able to suppress chitin-triggered immunity in the tomato cell suspension assay.
source_text: We confirmed that the Ecp6 protein produced in mammalian cells was able to suppress chitin-triggered immunity in the tomato cell suspension assay
evidence_reasoning: This is confirmed by the alkalinization assay data shown in Figure 6.

claim: HEK293-produced Ecp6 showed two binding sites for chitin with different affinities.
source_text: Lines in the lower panel represent best-fit curves for one (P. pastoris-produced T95R) or two (HEK293-produced) binding site model.
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from the ITC data fitting in Figure 7 requiring a two-site binding model.

claim: The LysM1-LysM3 composite binding site has a dissociation constant in the picomolar range.
source_text: the LysM1–LysM3 composite binding site has a dissociation constant in the picomolar range
evidence_reasoning: This is determined from ITC measurements of HEK293-produced chitin-free Ecp6 (Figure 7).

claim: LysM2 has a dissociation constant of 4.5 µM for chitin binding.
source_text: LysM2 has a dissociation constant of 4.5 µM
evidence_reasoning: This is determined from ITC measurements shown in Figure 7.

claim: The picomolar affinity of the LysM1-LysM3 binding site is approximately 1 million times higher than that of LysM2.
source_text: Thus, the picomolar affinity of the LysM1–LysM3 binding site is approximately 1 million times higher than that of LysM2
evidence_reasoning: This is calculated from the measured dissociation constants of the two binding sites.

claim: The ultra-high affinity of the LysM1-LysM3 composite binding site explains how LysM effectors outcompete plant host receptors for chitin binding.
source_text: The composite LysM1–LysM3 binding site shows ultra-high chitin-binding affinity, thus explaining how LysM effectors outcompete plant host receptors for chitin binding.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from the measured ultra-high affinity data combined with knowledge of plant receptor affinities.

claim: Various fungal pathogens secrete LysM effectors to scavenge chitin fragments and avoid recognition by host immune receptors.
source_text: Various fungal pathogens secrete LysM effectors to scavenge chitin fragments and thus avoid recognition by host immune receptors that activate immune responses
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations (de Jonge et al., 2010; Marshall et al., 2011; Mentlak et al., 2012) and represents established knowledge.

claim: The global arrangement of LysMs in the AtCERK1 ectodomain does not allow formation of an intrachain LysM dimer.
source_text: In contrast to Ecp6 (A), the global arrangement of the LysMs (colored in three shades of blue and with chitin-binding loops in red and green) in the AtCERK1 ectodomain does not allow the formation of an intrachain LysM dimer (B).
evidence_reasoning: This is based on comparison of the Ecp6 structure with the published AtCERK1 structure (Liu et al., 2012).

claim: AtCERK1 receptors bind in tandem to long chitin oligomers, prompting dimerization and activation of immune signaling.
source_text: In Arabidopsis, AtCERK1 receptors have been suggested to bind in tandem to long chitin oligomers, prompting dimerization and activation of immune signaling (Liu et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This is based on the model proposed by Liu et al., 2012.

claim: P. pastoris-produced Ecp6 can suppress chitin-triggered immunity even though only LysM2 is available for chitin binding.
source_text: In this study as well as in previous studies (de Jonge et al., 2010), it was found that P. pastoris-produced Ecp6 is able to suppress chitin-triggered immunity of tomato cells although only LysM2 is available for chitin binding.
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by the alkalinization assay data and confirmed by previous studies.

claim: The affinity of LysM2 for chitin is lower than previously determined affinities for chitin binding by tomato cells.
source_text: In this respect it is surprising that the affinity that was determined for chitin binding by LysM2 is lower than previously determined affinities for chitin binding by tomato cells (Baureithel et al., 1994).
evidence_reasoning: This comparison is made between the measured LysM2 affinity and published data from Baureithel et al., 1994.

claim: At the concentrations used in the alkalinization experiment, P. pastoris-produced Ecp6 will only sequester a small portion of available chitin oligosaccharides.
source_text: Because the concentrations of P. pastoris-produced Ecp6 (100 nM) and chitin (10 nM) that were used in the alkalinization experiment are much lower than the LysM2 dissociation constant (4.5 µM), P. pastoris-produced Ecp6 will only sequester a small portion of the available chitin oligosaccharides
evidence_reasoning: This is inferred from comparing the experimental concentrations to the measured dissociation constant.

claim: LysM2 may suppress chitin-triggered immunity by preventing immune receptor dimerization required for activation of immune signaling.
source_text: Potentially, LysM2 may be involved in perturbation of the activation of chitin-triggered immunity by preventing the immune receptor dimerization that is required for the activation of immune signaling (Liu et al., 2012).
evidence_reasoning: This is explicitly stated as a potential mechanism ('Potentially', 'may') inferred from the data and knowledge of receptor activation.

claim: Ecp6 may bind to chitin oligomers already bound by host immune receptor monomers, physically blocking receptor dimerization.
source_text: Ecp6 may bind to chitin oligomers that have been bound by host immune receptor monomers, thus physically blocking host immune receptor dimerization.
evidence_reasoning: This is explicitly stated as a speculative mechanism ('may') to explain the observed suppression of immunity.

claim: C. fulvum LysM effector Ecp6 suppresses chitin-triggered immunity through two mechanisms: chitin sequestration via LysM1-LysM3 and perturbation of host immune receptor complexes via LysM2.
source_text: In conclusion, it appears that the C. fulvum LysM effector Ecp6 is able to suppress chitin-triggered immunity through two mechanisms; efficient chitin oligosaccharide sequestration through a ligand-induced composite LysM1–LysM3 binding groove, and secondly a mechanism exerted by LysM2 that does not involve chitin oligosaccharide sequestration but may involve perturbation of host immune receptor complexes.
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion integrates the structural and functional data with speculative mechanisms for LysM2 function.

claim: Convergent evolution towards recognition of the same ligand by molecules of taxonomically diverse organisms frequently occurs.
source_text: Convergent evolution towards recognition of the same ligand by molecules of taxonomically diverse organisms frequently occurs, as exemplified by the perception of bacterial flagellin by the mammalian and plant immune receptors TLR5 and FLS2
evidence_reasoning: This is a general principle illustrated with cited examples (Felix et al., 1999; Smith et al., 2003; Chinchilla et al., 2006).

claim: Mammalian TLR5 and plant FLS2 recognize different PAMP motifs within bacterial flagellin.
source_text: as exemplified by the perception of bacterial flagellin by the mammalian and plant immune receptors TLR5 and FLS2, although these receptors recognize different PAMP motifs within the same ligand
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by citations to Felix et al., 1999; Smith et al., 2003; Chinchilla et al., 2006.

claim: Convergent evolution has brought about different modes to interact with the same PAMP motif in chitin perception by LysM proteins in taxonomically diverse organisms.
source_text: In contrast, our study on chitin perception by LysM proteins shows that convergent evolution has brought about different modes to interact with the same PAMP motif in taxonomically diverse organisms by structurally diverse proteins
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is inferred from comparing the Ecp6 structure and binding mechanism with that of plant receptors like AtCERK1.

source_text: A pPIC9 vector (Invitrogen) containing His6-FLAG tagged Ecp6 was used to express Ecp6 in Pichia pastoris (de Jonge et al., 2010).
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct description of the experimental method used.

claim: Large single crystals of Ecp6 were obtained by micro-seeding.
source_text: Large single crystals were only obtained by micro-seeding.

evidence_reasoning: This describes the experimental data collection method.

claim: Ecp6 has the potential to instantly and strongly bind chitin after secretion by fungal cells.
